summary: Require distinct declared execution units and deterministic bounded-handoff chaining for credited Adaptive Execution passes, then revalidate the merged Adaptive Execution behavior under the corrected discipline.
reason: PR #5 revision 6 recorded five SEPARATED semantic stages as complete even though they were effectively evaluated within one assistant response. The correction adds deterministic enforcement of unique declared execution-unit/boundary identities, ordered handoff chaining, closed historical exemptions, gate-before-pass chronology, historical identity uniqueness, immutable completed-pass evidence, current artifact-state binding for partial subdivided completion, and revision-bound redo semantics. Revision-8 Adversarial has now found and corrected six successive defects or assurance gaps: omission of the PR base snapshot from historical identity checks; mutation of execution identity after durable completion; inability to represent subdivided execution honestly because subpasses were only recognized after enclosing-stage credit; failure to validate a partial subpass completion against the current governed artifact state before its handoff could be consumed; a mapped pass-boundary evaluation specification that still described the older credited-pass model; and the ability to replace a durably completed logical pass with a different gate and new execution identities in the same review revision because gate_sha was part of the historical occurrence identity. The sixth finding is already covered by post-credit immutability and reopening semantics. Historical validation now permits only one completed occurrence per logical slot (review_revision, stage, pass_id); a redo after durable completion requires incrementing review_revision. Regression coverage and the mapped evaluation explicitly test that requirement. The gate used for this Adversarial attempt became stale when governed files changed and has been discarded. Adversarial remains uncredited pending a fresh retry. The repository still does not claim to prove a ChatGPT message/context boundary unless the host supplies a trustworthy boundary ID.
